title: Extension of a small-etale module morphism to cartesian families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $X$ an algebraic space over $S$, and $P,Q$ etale line presentations [def-trf-cartesian-line-presentation]. For every morphism $f:P.\mathrm{line}\to Q.\mathrm{line}$ of their specified small-etale modules, there is a cartesian family morphism $e:P\to Q$ inducing $f$ on all small-etale global sections. The map need not be an isomorphism. No uniqueness is asserted.

source.place: Tags 03G7 and 03M3; descent.tex Tags 03DX, 03LC, 023T and 05VG. The atlas argument and its morphism argument are specialized to rank one.

proof.text: Fix a small-etale test T. On every open U of T, identify the sections of P_T and Q_T with the sections on the open test using the tensor-to-open comparison [new-etale-tensor-open-section-iso] and the cartesian comparisons. Conjugate the component of f on that open test by the two specified section equivalences. These are additive, linear maps. Their restrictions commute by etaleSections_naturality, coherence and [new-etale-tensor-open-section-naturality]. Thus they form an ordinary module map on T. The Zariski/etale Hom comparison, [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison], shows that these chart maps commute with all further etale scheme maps, not only open inclusions.

For an arbitrary test W, pull back an etale surjective atlas of X. The resulting cover B of W maps to an etale test T. Pull back the chart map on T and conjugate by the two cartesian identifications for B to T. On the double overlap of B over W, both maps agree: they are pullbacks of the two chart maps to the atlas double overlap, where the preceding etale naturality identifies them. This is a morphism between the canonical descent data of P_W and Q_W. Both are invertible, hence quasi-coherent. Fullness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] descends this map to W.

For a test map j, compare the two composites in the required cartesian naturality equation after the pulled-back atlas. The defining atlas identification, the chart naturality and the coherence of P and Q make them equal there. Faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] proves equality on the source test. On a small-etale test the descended map equals the chart map by the same faithfulness, so it induces f on global sections. Empty tests and the zero morphism require no additional hypothesis.

theorem exists_testLineHom {X : AlgebraicSpace S} (P Q : EtaleLinePresentation X)
    (f : P.line ⟶ Q.line) :
    ∃ e : TestLineHom P.toTestLineFamily Q.toTestLineFamily,
      e.IsEtaleCompatible P Q f
